features: Important — This update changes the database: two migrations add the new tax-regime fields to the supplier record (withholding regime, recipient's legal nature, flat-rate scheme, etc.) and a flag to the invoice line to exclude it from the withholding calculation base. No existing data is touched: already-configured suppliers are recognised automatically where possible, otherwise they are left exactly as they were. Run the migrations after updating.

Withholding tax, a more precise supplier record: a supplier now has a withholding regime (works contracts 4%, self-employment 20%, agency commissions, non-residents) distinct from the recipient's legal nature (individual vs. corporate) — the latter alone now decides the tax code (1019 or 1020), instead of one field to fill in by hand. A supplier under the flat-rate scheme no longer needs to be configured to exclude withholding: the system knows and never applies it, whatever else is set. The legacy fields (percentage, tax code) remain valid as a manual override.

A supplier can issue both invoices subject to withholding and invoices that are not — think of someone who sells a fire extinguisher (not subject) and also services it (subject). When recording an invoice you can now switch off withholding for that single document, stating why (bank transfer with tax code already withheld, out of scope, incidental installation, flat-rate scheme, other), and exclude a specific line from the calculation base — typically the professional fund contribution, which by law never enters it.

The VAT rate proposed for a new invoice line is no longer fixed at 22%: it now defaults to the last rate used for the selected supplier, so bank charges stay at 0%, building trades at 10% and professionals at 22% without having to correct it by hand every time.

Fixed five defects in the withholding calculation: switching it off on an invoice wasn't saved by the registration form; reversing an invoice with withholding left an open residual on the Treasury account instead of reversing it along with the rest; a genuine credit note on a withholding-subject supplier still computed a deduction the preview never showed; the journal note always read "4%" even when the real rate was different; the professional fund contribution was wrongly pulled into the calculation base.

If a supplier has a withholding regime set but no recipient legal nature on file, the system cannot decide whether the tax code is 1019 or 1020: recording the invoice is now blocked with a warning and a direct link to complete the supplier record, unless you explicitly confirm you want to proceed anyway.
